props.gloss_en: the mishna: one who comes after nefalim, even though [the nefel] put out its head alive, is a firstborn for inheritance and not for the priest
the mishna: and [one who comes after] a nine-month [fetus] that put out its head dead

the mishna: [one who had no sons married a woman who gave birth] while still a gentile and converted, and when she came to Israel she gave birth -- that son is a firstborn for inheritance and not for the priest
R' Yosei HaGelili: [that son] is a firstborn for inheritance AND for the priest, as it says 'that opens the womb in Israel' (Ex 13:2) -- until they open a womb from Israel
R' Yosei HaGelili: from 'that opens the womb in Israel' -- until they open a womb from Israel
the mishna: [a woman who] converted while pregnant -- her son is a firstborn for the priest and not for inheritance
the mishna: she gave birth together with a kohenet, [or] with a Levite woman [and the sons were mixed up] -- a firstborn for the priest and not for inheritance
Shmuel: [emergence of] the head does not exempt in the case of nefalim
the reason: 'all in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life' (Gen 7:22)
wherever there is breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils, its head counts
the other [one without breath of life] -- its head does not count
the stam's answer: what is 'its head' [in the mishna's nefel clause]? most of it
the reason [the next is a firstborn for inheritance] is that its head emerged dead; had its head emerged alive, the one after it would not be a firstborn for inheritance either
the Chullin mishna: [a fetus that] put out its head, even though it withdrew it, is as born
[a human] cannot be learned from an animal, for it has no prozdor
an animal cannot be learned from a human, because a human's countenance is significant
the Nidda mishna: [a child] emerging in the usual way [is born] once most of its head has emerged; and what is most of its head? once its forehead emerges
Reish Lakish: the forehead [emerging] exempts everywhere
Reish Lakish: except for inheritance
the reason: the Merciful One said 'he shall recognize' (Deut 21:17)
R' Yochanan: [the forehead exempts] even for inheritance
'everywhere' comes to include the baraita's case of the convert
the baraita: a convert whose child's forehead emerged while she was a gentile and then converted -- she is not given the days of impurity and days of purity
the baraita: and she does not bring a birth offering
the baraita: 'he shall recognize' -- this is recognition of the face; and what is recognition of the face? the countenance with the nose
the mishna: one testifies [to a man's death] only on [seeing] the countenance with the nose
the baraita: forehead without countenance, countenance without forehead -- one does not testify until both are [seen] with the nose
Abaye (and some say Rav Kahana): what is the verse? 'the recognition of their faces witnesses against them' (Isa 3:9)
the stam's answer: testimony [freeing] a woman is different, for the Rabbis were stringent with it
the mishna: they established [the practice] of permitting [a woman] to marry on the testimony of a witness from a witness, a woman, a slave, a maidservant
the stam's second answer: 'he shall recognize' is one thing and recognition of the face [for testimony] another
R' Yochanan: one who had sons as a gentile and converted has no firstborn for inheritance
Reish Lakish: he has a firstborn for inheritance
for he has already had 'the first of his strength' (Deut 21:17)
[for inheritance:] a convert who converted is like a child just born
and they follow their [same] reasoning [in the pru urvu dispute]
R' Yochanan: [the convert who had sons as a gentile] has fulfilled pru urvu
Reish Lakish: he has not fulfilled [it]
fulfilled -- 'He did not create it a waste; He formed it to be inhabited' (Isa 45:18)
[for pru urvu:] not fulfilled -- a convert who converted is like a child just born

the pru-urvu dispute is needed: from the inheritance case alone one would say Reish Lakish rules so only because as gentiles they are not subject to inheritance, and concedes to R' Yochanan on pru urvu (לשבת יצרה, and he has made it inhabited)
the inheritance dispute is needed: from pru urvu alone one would say R' Yochanan rules so only there, and concedes to Reish Lakish on inheritance
no -- the mishna's case is truly [a son] from an Israelite who had no sons; [the gentile/maidservant] was needed for 'is not a firstborn for the priest'
[the clause 'not a firstborn for the priest'] excludes R' Yosei HaGelili's view: it teaches that [he is] not
the baraita: one who had sons as a gentile and converted has a firstborn for inheritance
Ravina (and some say Rav Acha): this [baraita] is certainly R' Yosei HaGelili's
and he learns his [the male convert's] case from hers [the female convert's]
Rav Adda bar Ahava: a Levite woman who gave birth -- her son is exempt from the five selaim
it is written 'by their families, by their fathers' houses' (Num 1:2) -- lineage follows the father
Rav Pappa: [Rav Adda's case is] where she became pregnant from a gentile
Rav Pappa: not only for the view that the child is not blemished; even for the view that it is, he is called a disqualified Levite
Mar brei d'Rav Yosef in Rava's name: actually she became pregnant from an Israelite, and there it is different
for the verse says 'opens the womb' (Ex 13:2): the Merciful One made it depend on the opening of the womb
by implication [of the mishna], a kohenet and a Levite woman [their sons] are exempt
the son of a kohenet who became pregnant from a gentile is exempt [from the five selaim]
Rav Pappa [to Rabba]: is this not Rav Adda bar Ahava's case -- a Levite woman who gave birth, her son is exempt?
Rabba: granted, a Levite woman remains in her sanctity
the baraita: a Levite woman who was captured or had illicit intercourse -- she is given tithe and eats
Rabba: but a kohenet -- once he has intercourse with her she becomes a non-priestess
it works for Mar brei d'Rav Yosef in Rava's name: he sets the mishna where she became pregnant from an Israelite
actually she became pregnant from a priest and is herself an Israelite; she is called kohenet because her son is a priest
Rav Chisda: a priest who died and left a chalal son -- the son must redeem himself
Rabba bar Rav Huna: he need not redeem himself
where the father died after thirty days, all agree the son need not redeem himself
for his father has acquired his redemption [money]
where they disagree is when the father died within thirty days
within thirty days, the son must redeem himself
for his father did not acquire his redemption [money]
within thirty days, the son need not redeem himself
for he can say [to the priest]: I come by the power of a man with whom you could not litigate

objections.gloss_en: ומי אחמירו? והא תנן: הוחזקו להיות משיאים עד מפי עד, מפי אשה, מפי עבד, מפי שפחה!

answered_by.gloss_en: כי אקילו רבנן בסופה, בתחלתה לא אקילו -- lenient about who reports, not about the identification itself

objections.gloss_en: תנן ... עודה גויה ונתגיירה ... ולדה בכור לנחלה. ילדה ממאן? אילימא מישראל שלא היו לו בנים -- מאי איריא גיורת ושפחה? אלא לאו מגר שהיו לו בנים ונתגייר, וקתני בכור לנחלה! (47a.7-8)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, לעולם מישראל שלא היו לו בנים, ואינו בכור לכהן איצטריכא ליה -- לאפוקי מדרבי יוסי הגלילי (47a.10; = p_leolam_miyisrael, p_leafukei_ryhg)

objections.gloss_en: תא שמע: היו לו בנים בגיותו ונתגייר -- יש לו בכור לנחלה!

answered_by.gloss_en: הא ודאי רבי יוסי הגלילי היא ... ויליף איהו מינה דידה (= p_ravina_ryhg, p_ravina_yalif_mina; ואיתימא רב אחא)

objections.gloss_en: דאיעבר ממאן? אילימא מכהן ומלוי -- מאי איריא לויה? אפילו ישראלית נמי! אלא דאיעבר מישראל -- למשפחתם לבית אבתם כתיב! (47a.13)

answered_by.gloss_en: דאיעבר מגוי (= p_pappa_migoy), and even for מזהמין -- לוי פסול מיקרי
משמיה דרבא: לעולם מישראל, ושאני התם דאמר קרא פטר רחם -- בפטר רחם תלא רחמנא (= p_mar_miyisrael, p_mar_peter_rechem)

objections.gloss_en: הכי השתא?! בשלמא לויה בקדושתה קיימא ... אלא כהנת, כיון דאי בעיל לה הויא זרה -- the two cases are not alike

תנן ... וילדה היא וכהנת היא ולויה היא ... בכור לכהן -- מכלל דכהנת ולויה פטורין (47a.18); from a priest or Levite, why name them? from a gentile -- is a kohenet's son exempt? Rabba showed she becomes zara (47a.19-21); so the mishna is from an Israelite -- הניחא למר (47a.22), אלא לרב פפא במאי מוקי לה?

answered_by.gloss_en: לעולם דאיעבר מכהן, והיא בת ישראל; ואמאי קרי לה כהנת? דבנה כהן (= p_kohenet_dbena_kohen)

objections.gloss_en: תנן: נתגיירה מעוברת -- בכור לכהן. ואמאי? לימא ליה: אתינא מכח גברא דלא מצית לאשתעויי דינא בהדיה!

answered_by.gloss_en: שאני גוי דלית ליה חייס -- a gentile has no lineage, so the son does not come by his father's power
